title: The Compass of Nagasaki's harbor
premise: In 1866 Nagasaki, August Dravenmoor, daughter of a Dutch-trained typeface cutter, works in her father's print shop on the harbor's edge as anti-shogunate unrest boils over. When her father secretly prints a pamphlet proving a loyalist faction massacred a village and blamed foreign sailors, the shogunate's inspectors seal the only bridge out of the city for the season, trapping them with the evidence. August must carry the type-set proof past three checkpoints to a Dutch ship before the harbor freezes of official traffic — discovering along the way that her father printed the pamphlet knowing it would doom him, a final act of truth over loyalty. She succeeds at terrible cost: her father is taken, the shop burns, and August sails from Nagasaki carrying not just the evidence but a new identity she chose for herself.
about_author: Vesper Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing merchant letters from treaty-port Japan. They write historical fiction about ordinary people caught in the machinery of upheaval.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: August Dravenmoor's POV. In the family print shop above Nagasaki's harbor, August sorts type while her father cuts new faces by lamplight. She measures her life in what can be carried — a habit from her mother's flight years ago. Emotional beat: quiet competence masking restlessness.

chapters.title: Rumors in the Fish Market
chapters.summary: August hears whispers of massacred villages and blamed foreigners while buying ink supplies. Her friend Kenji, a dock clerk, warns her to stop asking questions. Emotional beat: the first crack in her belief that paper and truth are harmless.

chapters.title: The Locked Drawer
chapters.summary: August discovers a hidden galley of set type and a printed proof describing the massacre — implicating a faction her father has quietly supported for years. POV shifts briefly to the father, torn. Emotional beat: betrayal blooming into dread.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Father explains nothing; he only says some truths must outlive their printers. August confronts him; he refuses to name his allies. Emotional beat: the rupture between daughter and father, love strained against principle.

chapters.title: Orders Come
chapters.summary: Shogunal inspectors arrive unannounced. Father hides the proofs inside a shipment of blank ledgers. August watches him lie smoothly for the first time in her life. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Official notice: the land bridge is sealed for the season after an assassination attempt. The city becomes a cage. August realizes the evidence cannot leave by road — only by ship, and ships require passes. Emotional beat: claustrophobia and the ticking clock established.

chapters.title: Kenji's Price
chapters.summary: August asks Kenji for harbor access. He agrees, but his price is dangerous: she must copy shipping manifests that could hang his own brother. Emotional beat: complicity — everyone in Nagasaki is now smuggling something.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Paper Gate
chapters.summary: August carries proofs sewn into her coat lining through the customs house. An inspector who once bought type from her father lingers too long over her papers. Emotional beat: terror rendered in small mercies.

chapters.title: The Dutch Factor
chapters.summary: August approaches the trading house of Hendrik Vosse, a factor who owes her father old debts. He agrees to take the documents aboard the next outbound ship — but wants the original type blocks as well, to sell the story twice. Emotional beat: hope complicated by greed.

chapters.title: A Night of Fires
chapters.summary: Loyalist cells torch government storehouses across the quarter. In the chaos, the print shop is searched again. Father sends August away; she sleeps in the type loft, listening to the city burn. Emotional beat: the revolution arriving at her doorstep.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Harbor Watch
chapters.summary: Kenji forges a pass, but the watch sergeant knows his handwriting. August improvises, claiming the bundle is funeral goods for a drowned sailor. POV alternates with the sergeant, who suspects but lets her pass for reasons of his own. Emotional beat: survival by performance.

chapters.title: The Brother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Kenji delivers the copied manifests; August learns his brother is among the massacre's perpetrators. She must decide whether to include his name in the evidence. Emotional beat: loyalty versus truth made flesh in one choice.

chapters.title: What My Mother Carried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: August remembers her mother fleeing with only a typecase and a story half-told. She finally understands the habit of measuring the world in what can be carried. Emotional beat: inheritance of survival, grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Vosse's Bargain
chapters.summary: Vosse raises his price: he wants exclusive publication rights and August's silence about how he profits from scandal. She signs, hating herself, knowing the truth will reach the world slightly bent. Emotional beat: the corrupting arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: The Denunciation
chapters.summary: An informer names the print shop. Soldiers come at dawn; father burns the remaining type rather than let it be used for lies, and is arrested. August watches from the crowd, unrecognized. Emotional beat: devastation, and the terrible clarity that follows.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Ship's Ladder
chapters.summary: With the harbor under scrutiny, August must board the Dutch vessel herself. Disguised as a laundress, she climbs the ladder with the proofs hidden in wet linen. A guard grabs her sleeve. Emotional beat: the climax's threshold — everything balanced on one grip.

chapters.title: The Hold
chapters.summary: Below decks, August hides among cargo as soldiers search the ship. She clutches the proofs and thinks of her father's hands cutting letterforms. The search passes inches away. Emotional beat: held breath, prayer without religion.

chapters.title: Departure
chapters.summary: The ship weighs anchor as August watches Nagasaki shrink — the bridge, the smoke, the shop's charred sign. She has the evidence but no plan for herself. Vosse offers her passage onward as his 'typographer.' Emotional beat: exile and strange freedom entwined.

chapters.title: The Interrogation
chapters.summary: POV shift: in a cell, August's father refuses to name her, claiming he acted alone. His interrogator, himself a printer's son, quietly delays the paperwork. Emotional beat: unexpected mercy inside the machine of punishment.

chapters.title: The Pamphlet Appears
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the evidence surfaces in treaty ports and foreign papers; the massacre can no longer be denied. August reads her father's typeface in a printed page and weeps. Emotional beat: vindication that tastes like ash.

chapters.title: What Cannot Be Carried
chapters.summary: August returns secretly to Nagasaki one last time, bribing her way past the still-closed bridge. She finds the shop's ruins and leaves a single cut letterform on the scorched sill — her father's mark. Emotional beat: mourning, and letting go.

chapters.title: A New Face
chapters.summary: Aboard a ship bound for Batavia, August cuts her first original typeface and signs the trial sheet with a name she chose herself. The compass of the harbor points outward now. Emotional beat: resolution — identity forged, truth delivered, survival paid for and accepted.
